frictions.description: The round-2 defect path (a client revalidating its cached availability with If-None-Match and keeping the stale body) could not be reproduced from the browser itself in this session: the pre-change plain reload and the post-change plain reload both issued fresh requests with NO If-None-Match header and got 200s, i.e. agent-browser's Chrome did not serve the disk-cached body across a reload here. So the plain reload alone cannot distinguish "the fix works" from "the browser never cached".
frictions.resolution: Kept the plain reload as the primary guest-channel check (it renders the correct closed state, no chips, 200) and added two labelled mechanism proofs on the exact round-2 defect path: (1) curl replay of the pre-change ETag `If-None-Match: "0.68.11"` -> now 200 with the new body/ETag (round 2: 304 + stale body); (2) an in-page `fetch(url)` with the browser DEFAULT cache mode (no cache option, not a bypass) -> online_closed/0 slots (round 2: stale 36-slot body). Both label the browser's If-None-Match absence honestly in the report.

frictions.description: The parent's step-2 text says the operator availability 'must return 0 slots with the online-closed state', but the live endpoint returns 141 slots with dayState.state='online_closed' (staff channel unaffected). 0 operator slots is what the CLOSED day returns (verified in step 3).
